ACTIVE PUBLIC CONTRACT — October 13, 2026.
The signed MiMo opening is live from global epoch 189. This guide describes
the new model run; older contracts apply only to their historical epochs.

Scoring notice (2026-10-23): LIVE on-chain weights use **flip-incentive** scoring
(https://affine.io/scores.json) with a TOPLOC/sampling verify gate: verify **fail**
strips flip credit and excludes the batch from GRPO packing. Unverified earns
nothing. No authenticity *bonus*. Never all-zero weights (last-good share floor).
See “Flip-incentive LIVE scoring — October 23, 2026” below. The MiMo
complete-group mining contract (nonces 0–7, mixed correct/wrong) is unchanged.

## Flip-incentive LIVE scoring — October 23, 2026

**Status: LIVE.** On-chain mech-0 weights are set from the flip+surprise formula.
The MiMo complete-group mining contract (8-nonce groups, nonces 0–7, mixed
correct/wrong) is **unchanged**; no new miner client is required. This gate does
**not** strip nonce or mixed-outcome admission.

### TOPLOC / sampling verify gate (2026-10-23)

| Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| TOPLOC or sampling verify **fail** | No flip credit on that batch/traj **and** do not pack into GRPO |
| Unverified / unaudited / pending | Earns **nothing** and is **not** packed into GRPO |
| Verify scope | **All** batches that can earn flip credit or enter GRPO (not spot-check-only) |
| No authenticity *bonus* | `no_authenticity_guard=true` — formula has no separate authenticity term |
| Tolerances | Unchanged — do not loosen TOPLOC / logprob tolerances |
| Never all-zero weights | If authenticity / unknown_policy would zero all shares, retain last-good shares (or refuse submit and keep on-chain). Never burn. Never owner-only. |

Public scores metadata: `formula.sampling_verify_gate` on https://affine.io/scores.json
(`fail_strips_credit`, `credit_requires_verify_pass`). Formula version:
`sn120-flip-incentive-live-v1`.

### What changed from v9 / seq7

| | Previous LIVE (v9 seq7) | LIVE now (flip) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| URL | https://affine.io/scores.json | https://affine.io/scores.json (same path) |
| Rule | window credit `groups × (1 − p)` over 4 epochs | fail→pass flip + surprise |
| On-chain / hourly writer | yes | yes (reads flip shares; never submits all-zero) |
| Refresh | after each hourly weight run | scores ~every 5 min; weights hourly |

`scores-shadow.json` may mirror the same flip document during transition.

### Formula (live v1)

For each published probe epoch pair `(E → E_next)` with private `per_task`:

1. **Join** miner `DISPATCH.payload.selected[]` at epoch `E` (`miner`, `index`)
   with probe `envs.affine_math.per_task[<index>]` at `E` and `E_next`.
2. **Eligibility (hard_fail):** baseline status at `E` ∈
   `{unresolved, wrong, error, mixed}` — credit only while the task was failing.
3. **Credit:** fail→pass ⇒ `+ surprise(p̂)` where `w = −log(max(p̂, ε))`, `ε=1e-4`.
4. **Debit:** pass→fail ⇒ `− surprise(1 − p̂)`.
5. **p̂:** running EMA of prior probe pass rates (`α=0.3`), else bandit `ema_p`,
   else raw pass at `E`, else `0.5`.
6. **Shares:** `relu(flip_score) / sum` over miners. No authenticity bonus.
   Verify-fail strips credit; unverified earns nothing when the verify ledger
   marks the batch. Share floor: never publish/submit an all-zero vector — retain
   last-good shares or keep on-chain weights. Unearned / unregistered mass that
   would otherwise burn is not used as a reason to submit zeros.

Window: published probe epochs with `epoch ≥ 93` (full 7,496-task pool). Formula
version field: `sn120-flip-incentive-live-v1`.

### Env probe (inputs)

- Continuous partial coverage + bounded bandit top-k sampling on `affine_math`.
- Index / series: https://affine.io/probe/index.json · https://affine.io/probe/series.json
- Real-time aggregates: https://affine.io/probe/c/
- Lagged full per-task dumps (after 2 sealed probe epochs): https://affine.io/probe/tasks/
- Flip scoring uses the private per-task stream immediately; the public
  `/probe/tasks/` lag is for audit.

### What miners should do

Keep submitting under the **October 13 MiMo complete-group contract** below.
Live weights reward recovering **failing** tasks (fail→pass) with higher surprise
on rare successes. Prefer frontier / currently-failing tasks; submission format,
nonces, runtime, and proof transport do not change. Batches that fail TOPLOC or
sampling verification earn no flip credit and are excluded from GRPO packing.
Unverified batches likewise earn no credit and are not trained on.

## What changes at this cutover

This is a new model run and a new miner contract. Upgrade the canonical client
and install the exact MiMo runtime before joining it. An old Qwen2.5-Math client
does not become compatible merely because a manifest changes. Custom miners
must implement the complete new contract and pass the same checks.

The new starting model is XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, upstream revision
2367e865d009c13ac81713a2878291d33ab28177. Its authenticated original checkpoint is
87de8304e9d33dde39b81a41fdbbf306426ea6fd993b7d85332e6a48e8a4bbae
(18,849,863,399 model-file bytes). Start this run with a fresh optimizer. Earlier
Qwen-model histories remain archived and are not a continuation of this run.
After each update miners use the new signed checkpoint, not the upstream base
again. A previously trained private rehearsal checkpoint is not the run genesis.

The activated task split is the existing 7,496 usable MATH problems, with
6,746 mining tasks and 750 reserved held-out tasks. The authenticated split
digest is recorded above. Only `environments[].indices` in the current signed
opening authorizes mining. Old task cooldowns are not implicitly carried into
this fresh run. Held-out tasks never become miner tasks or training inputs.

One task batch now contains the entire canonical group of eight attempts:

- Generate exactly nonces 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and submit them in that order.
- At least one attempt must be completed and correct, and at least one must be
  completed and wrong. There is no four-correct/four-wrong quota.
- Retain all eight original outcomes, including unresolved attempts. Do not
  replace an unfavorable attempt, omit a cap, add a nonce offset, try nonce 8,
  or generate a larger group and select eight members from it.
- If the whole group fails the two outcome minima, search another approved
  task. All-correct, all-wrong, and correct-plus-unresolved-only groups do not
  qualify. Native grader or infrastructure errors do not supply a wrong answer.
- Different prescribed attempts may legitimately produce identical output
  tokens. Preserve them with their distinct bound nonce identities. Repeating
  a nonce or claiming the same committed group twice is not allowed.
- The initial cap remains nine eligible task batches per registered UID per
  epoch. One group is one task contribution, not eight separate contributions.

Parallel execution of attempts is allowed. Ordered nonces describe the required
sampling challenges and submitted group, not provable wall-clock execution order.
Task search and mixed-group admission still condition the training distribution;
they do not establish unbiased coverage of every task.

## Runtime, sampling and completed answers

Use the exact approved source, checkpoint files, tokenizer, chat template,
runtime fingerprint and signed numerical profile. The architecture is Qwen3.5
hybrid attention, with BF16 model parameters and FP32 recurrent state. It is not
the previous all-FP32 Qwen2.5 generation path. Initial qualification is for the
explicitly admitted H200/SM90 runtime; another GPU or kernel stack requires its
own qualification.

Generate through the released `cached_sample` / `MimoRuntime` path, with a fresh
cache for each trajectory. The qualified path executes one sequence per model
forward pass. Independent replicas may run in parallel; combining trajectories
into a different tensor batch or substituting another inference engine is not
covered by that qualification. Full-prefill logits used for proof construction
are not interchangeable with the prescribed cached generation distribution.
Do not override attention, recurrent precision or global numerical settings.
When reporting a rejection, include epoch/task/nonce, client release, GPU,
driver, PyTorch distribution/build, and any generation-path changes; no keys.

The new manifest uses:
- Runtime: `qwen3_5-mimo-v1`.
- Sampling: `forced-inverse-cdf-complete-group-mimo-v1`.
- Harness: `text-tools-mimo-complete-group-v1`.
- Temperature1, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, thinking enabled, eager attention.
- Approved stop-token IDs `[248046, 248044]`; stop at the first approved EOS.
- Up to 8,192 generated tokens and 12,288 total context tokens initially.
  The signed opening is authoritative; a prompt plus its full output horizon
  must fit. Do not silently truncate prompts or change generation limits.

Draws bind run, epoch randomness, checkpoint content, miner identity, native task,
canonical prompt, group size, nonce, turn and token position, along with the
versioned sampler/runtime settings. Download URLs are refreshable capabilities;
they are excluded from checkpoint content identity and do not change the draws.
An old proof cannot establish validity under a new checkpoint or challenge.

The final-answer policy is `mimo-final-channel-math-v1`. With thinking enabled,
a properly framed `<think>...</think>` channel precedes the final channel. The
native math grader evaluates the completed boxed answer in that final channel.
A box inside reasoning does not supply the final answer. The full original
reasoning and final token sequence remains in the proof and training document.
A correct final answer does not prove that every reasoning step is correct.

Budget-capped outputs are unresolved, including outputs containing an earlier
box. EOS outputs without a gradeable final answer, missing/empty/unbalanced final
boxes, or invalid final-channel framing are also unresolved. They satisfy neither
outcome minimum. Native grader failures are indeterminate infrastructure outcomes,
not invented negative examples.

## Registration and key safety

### Null consensus and PoW registration — October 13, 2026

Subnet 120 now uses Null consensus, and proof-of-work (PoW) registration is
enabled. Both changes are finalized on Finney. Burned registration remains
available. The subnet capacity was subsequently increased to 1,000 UIDs;
this is a registration capacity, not a claim that all slots are occupied.

PoW difficulty was reset to 100,000,000, with a minimum of 100,000,000.
This is computational difficulty, not a TAO fee. Difficulty is dynamic: the
existing demand adjustment raises it after PoW registrations and decays it
toward the minimum. The current controls are a 1.5x increase multiplier and
a 720-block half-life. Read live chain values before mining a registration
proof; do not assume difficulty stays at its initial 100-million value.

Use a current Bittensor CLI with PoW support and your intended wallet/hotkey:

```sh
btcli subnets register --netuid 120 --pow
```

PoW obtains a subnet UID; it does not replace Affine activation below. Use an
Ed25519 mining hotkey compatible with Affine. Registration still follows the
chain's capacity, pruning and immunity rules; solving PoW does not reserve a
free slot or guarantee permanent registration.

Under Null consensus, only the highest-stake registered validator holds the
weight-setting permit. At activation this is Affine's existing UID 0 writer.
The hourly best-assessment writer continues to distribute miner weights;
the complete eight-trajectory batch contract and GRPO training recipe remain
unchanged. No miner client upgrade is required solely for this consensus change;
PoW registration itself requires a CLI supporting that registration route.

Finalized chain receipts:
- Null consensus: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9276975-0011
- PoW enabled: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9276978-0026
- Minimum difficulty 100,000,000: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9276987-0005
- Difficulty reset to 100,000,000: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9276991-0003
- UID capacity increased to 1,000: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9277005-0008

The live runtime accepted both difficulty changes through the subnet owner's
Owner proxy. Older guidance describing them as root-only is not accurate for
these finalized changes.

There is no operator whitelist. A miner needs a current subnet 120 UID, an
Ed25519 hotkey and a valid Affine activation. New openings snapshot eligible
identities; registration or activation during an epoch may take effect in the
next opening. A new model run does not itself require a new mining identity.

For an already registered Ed25519 hotkey, preview activation from the canonical
repository:

```sh
python -m subnet.register --wallet YOUR_WALLET --hotkey YOUR_ED25519_HOTKEY
```

Add `--execute` only when submitting the activation commitment. This command
does not buy or register a subnet UID. The mining key file contains the activated
32-byte Ed25519 seed as hexadecimal and must have mode 0600. Never disclose that
seed or a coldkey. Use one supervisor per identity/state directory; stop the old
miner before handing its state to an upgraded launcher.

## Install the new runtime and client

### Starting with zero TAO: register by PoW, then activate

You can start with zero TAO in both the coldkey and hotkey. The current Finney
runtime provides fee-free `pow_register`; Affine activation also has zero fees
and zero deposits. GPU rental, electricity and bandwidth still cost money.
PoW registration does not guarantee rewards: you must then submit eligible
complete task groups under the current epoch contract.

Use a separate registration environment. The approved MiMo mining runtime's
Bittensor 11.0.2 does not implement this new PoW route. Do not upgrade that
mining runtime in place. The following public SDK source was built and used
on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 H200 machine with Python 3.12, `uv`, GCC and pkg-config:

```sh
umask 077
mkdir -p pow-sdk
curl --fail --location --proto '=https' \
  https://github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor/archive/24e6b4daf911de4f300f3254f153db8ed274788d.tar.gz \
  --output pow-sdk/source.tar.gz
printf '%s  %s\n' \
  46482755edab0da685fe51e1e9fe2276e3856448713b8a8ee3dfcdb3440e312d \
  pow-sdk/source.tar.gz | sha256sum --check
tar -xzf pow-sdk/source.tar.gz -C pow-sdk --strip-components=1
uv venv --python 3.12 pow-env
uv pip install --python pow-env/bin/python ./pow-sdk/sdk/python
pow-env/bin/python -c 'import bittensor_core; print(bittensor_core.pow_gpu_devices())'
```

The matching native core builds from the pinned source. GPU PoW needs a working
NVIDIA OpenCL driver/ICD; CUDA availability alone does not establish that.
`--pow-backend auto` can use a supported GPU or fall back to CPU. A search timeout
means no proof was found within that attempt; it does not mean TAO is required.

Clone the canonical Affine repository, or update an existing checkout while
preserving private state. Replace `/absolute/affine` below with that checkout.
The registration helper is in current GitHub main; the approved mining worker
still comes from the immutable source archive identified above.
Create a fresh wallet with an Ed25519 hotkey and matching private mining seed:

```sh
mkdir -p private
pow-env/bin/python /absolute/affine/ops/create_ed25519_miner_wallet.py \
  --directory "$PWD/private/affine-wallet"
```

The helper refuses to overwrite an existing directory. It prints only public
identity information and paths; recovery phrases, wallet keys and `miner.seed`
stay in owner-only files. Back up that directory privately before terminating
the machine. Never publish it or copy its contents into logs or support messages.

Register the fresh hotkey on subnet 120 using PoW:

```sh
pow-env/bin/btcli subnets register \
  --netuid 120 --pow --pow-backend auto --pow-workers 8 --pow-timeout 900 \
  --network finney --wallet affine-pow --wallet-hotkey miner \
  --wallet-path "$PWD/private/affine-wallet/wallets" --yes --json
```

Keep `--pow`: the burned-registration route spends TAO. Use `--wallet-hotkey`
for the wallet's hotkey name in this CLI. A finalized registration supplies a
UID; it does not yet activate Affine mining. Activate the same identity:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/absolute/affine pow-env/bin/python -m subnet.register \
  --wallet affine-pow --hotkey miner \
  --wallet-path "$PWD/private/affine-wallet/wallets" \
  --network finney --netuid 120 --execute
```

Allow roughly three minutes for the activation commitment to reveal, then wait
for the next signed epoch roster to include the new identity. An already-open
epoch does not acquire new capabilities retroactively. Continue with the
separate approved MiMo runtime installation and mining command below, using
`--key /absolute/private/affine-wallet/miner.seed` adjusted to your actual path.
The supervisor follows signed public discovery and model handovers; miners do
not need an operator whitelist entry or private bucket credentials.

Qualification on October 13, 2026: a fresh rented H200 and unfunded wallet
registered as UID 256, then activated successfully. Both coldkey and hotkey
remained at zero free/reserved TAO. Registration and activation each paid zero
fees: https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9277113-0013 and
https://taomarketcap.com/extrinsics/9277117-0008. The test used the pinned SDK's
PoW and commitment calls with transaction journaling. Its first mining batch
is still awaiting admission in the next public epoch; registration success
alone is not evidence of an accepted rollout or earned reward.

### Approved mining runtime

Use the reviewed release commit above from https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine.
Preserve local work and private state when updating. The source approved by the
signed opening controls the actual child miner; arbitrary GitHub main contents
do not override it.

Permanent runtime artifact inventory:
https://affine.io/releases/mimo-runtime-20261013/ARTIFACTS.json
These artifacts were published as prepared assets; their availability alone
does not activate the new contract or replace the signed qualification scope.

```sh
mkdir -p /absolute/mimo-artifacts
MIMO_ARTIFACT_BASE=https://affine.io/releases/mimo-runtime-20261013
curl --fail --location --retry 3 --proto '=https' \
  "$MIMO_ARTIFACT_BASE/57442fdd51cf165c00ce4c531100aff3fc9f8a0a6ae43f4bf1868d5d0f912875/requirements.lock.txt" \
  --output /absolute/mimo-artifacts/requirements.lock.txt
curl --fail --location --retry 3 --proto '=https' \
  "$MIMO_ARTIFACT_BASE/84c8db262fd302d21eb52c151ab039071948d0002f3848b09cea53c750934205/toploc-0.1.6-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" \
  --output /absolute/mimo-artifacts/toploc-0.1.6-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl
sha256sum --check <<'SHA256'
57442fdd51cf165c00ce4c531100aff3fc9f8a0a6ae43f4bf1868d5d0f912875  /absolute/mimo-artifacts/requirements.lock.txt
84c8db262fd302d21eb52c151ab039071948d0002f3848b09cea53c750934205  /absolute/mimo-artifacts/toploc-0.1.6-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl
SHA256
python3 /absolute/affine/ops/bootstrap_mimo_runtime.py \
  --destination /absolute/mimo-runtime \
  --source-root /absolute/affine \
  --requirements /absolute/mimo-artifacts/requirements.lock.txt \
  --requirements-sha256 57442fdd51cf165c00ce4c531100aff3fc9f8a0a6ae43f4bf1868d5d0f912875 \
  --toploc-wheel /absolute/mimo-artifacts/toploc-0.1.6-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl \
  --toploc-wheel-sha256 84c8db262fd302d21eb52c151ab039071948d0002f3848b09cea53c750934205 \
  --python 3.12 --max-jobs 2
```

The runtime destination must be new. The installer checks the exact dependency
lock and native TOPLOC round trip; inspect `BOOTSTRAP.json`, `runtime-probe.json`
and `install.log`. The lock includes torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.14.1 and the rebuilt
TOPLOC 0.1.6 wheel. Do not substitute the separate `2.14.0+cu130` distribution or
an arbitrary PyPI TOPLOC binary. Do not add optional attention/recurrent kernels
or change numerical settings outside the admitted profile. Package versions
alone do not establish numerical compatibility.

## Start and continue mining

After the authenticated MiMo opening is active, run the upgraded supervisor using
the new runtime's Python from the reviewed repository. The command below uses
four independent B1 replicas on an admitted H200 with sufficient free memory:

```sh
CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 /absolute/mimo-runtime/venv/bin/python -B -m subnet.miner_supervisor \
  --discovery-url https://affine.io/mining.json \
  --authority 3301134b38401196d006a621ac4a772bb4b0e6afa15a7d34a0d1ae5f2c630bcd \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/mimo-approved-source \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.seed \
  --state /absolute/private/mimo-miner-state \
  --env-id affine_math --mimo-replicas 4
```

One replica is the default; two are also supported. Replica count is a local
compute setting and does not change group size, seeds, nonce order, deadlines
or reward limits. Runtime admission includes the memory required by the parent
and independent replicas. Do not point another active launcher at this state.

Omit `--max-batches` to follow the signed cap. An explicit smaller value is a
local limit. `--search-budget` is a local ceiling, not a nonce range: the legacy
value 32 permits a canonical N8 group but still generates exactly eight attempts.
A ceiling below N fails before generation; it does not produce partial groups.

The supervisor reads `accepting_submissions` and authenticates the signed current
pointer, opening, source and task assets against the fixed authority. It checks
HTTPS, archive membership/size and complete-file hashes, then launches the exact
approved child source once per epoch. Source URLs may use `url` or `read_url`;
both must agree if present. A website hint cannot authorize a different signed
epoch, extend a deadline or choose an unapproved checkpoint.

Checkpoint downloads are resumable and use up to four bounded transfers. Each
file must pass SHA256 before inference. Leave space for current and incoming
models. After a successor is admitted and the previous child has exited, the
supervisor retires only obsolete model caches it owns. Unknown pre-existing
files are preserved. No routine manual cache clearing is required for that path.

After this client/runtime upgrade, ordinary checkpoint changes are automatic:
the supervisor follows the next authenticated opening and starts a new child.
A future incompatible dependency or protocol change may still require an
explicit client/runtime upgrade. Signed source is not a security sandbox.

The complete-group journal preserves original attempts across interruption.
Keep its state and cumulative upload journal; do not reset them to seek a fresh
nonce window or duplicate credit. The supervisor does not blindly rerun an
already issued epoch after a child failure. Its inherited local lock prevents
overlapping children across a supervisor restart; it does not coordinate an
independent machine using the same identity.

## Proofs, uploads and rewards

Group transport is `complete-group-commitment-v1`, using compact bounded group
artifacts and `selected-token-logprobs-v1`. Upload the original tokens, selected
probabilities, sampler witness, TOPLOC fingerprints and native outcome metadata.
Do not upload full-vocabulary probability arrays. Full-vocabulary distributions
are recomputed by the verifier.

The client uploads immutable per-slot group/proof objects and compact training
documents, then updates a small signed cumulative commitment. Conditional writes
protect the original objects; an acknowledged group cannot be rewritten. Retry
the same bytes and preserve local prepared state. Encrypted per-miner capabilities
grant scoped upload/read rights; miners need no permanent R2 credentials and
cannot read other miners' private current submissions. `direct-r2-v1` on the
outer pointer describes storage access, not the inner proof format.

Sampling audits check the bound token path, TOPLOC and native outcomes. Fast
prefill disagreements receive the prescribed exact cached adjudication; numerical
ambiguity and infrastructure failure remain distinct from confirmed invalidity.
TOPLOC alone is not sampling verification. Passing token-path checks does not
prove original authorship, unique historical execution or correct reasoning.

The numerical profile uses strict zero acceptance thresholds; these are checking
limits, not a claim that cached and prefill outputs always agree. Its measured
calibration evidence is pinned by SHA256
e57c0f986cc56da6779d8e4c8a14266b0aae5964544dde2d2e3118ab35686b58.
The tested prefill disagreements required cached adjudication. Selected-logprob
and TOPLOC comparisons remain separate strict checks. Qualification covers the
admitted tested runtime, not every GPU implementation or possible exploit.

Continuous verifiers sample current and historical immutable groups independently
of the trainer. Rewards use native-eligible unique task contributions, accumulated
authenticated audit evidence and configured penalties. Groups excluded only by
the learner's compute budget can still contribute to rewards. The existing
cross-miner task-collision rule remains: submissions from multiple miners for the
same environment/task within an epoch receive zero uniqueness contribution. Cumulative retries never add credit. All eight outcomes
remain one task group for accounting.

The current global audit estimate counts authenticated invalid observations in
an eight-epoch window: an observation is recent when its global epoch is less
than eight rounds behind the latest admitted epoch. One recent invalid applies
an invalid-sample reward multiplier of 0.1; two or more apply zero. The signed
field is named `zero_epoch_after=2`, but this global estimator applies it across
the recent eight epochs, not only within one epoch. Three or more recent invalids
also activate the blacklist while the latest bad epoch is fewer than four rounds
old. The separate two-invalid zero rule can outlast that blacklist condition.
New submissions do not instantly erase these penalties. They are applied after
contribution smoothing, and historical overlap retains stricter admitted factors.

A fast prefill disagreement alone is not an invalid-sample penalty: the prescribed
cached adjudication checks the sampling path. Infrastructure failures do not
count as invalid samples. Numerically unresolved evidence is not proof of fraud;
where admitted as numerical ambiguity, it affects resolution coverage rather
than the invalid counter. An invalid-contract verdict does not establish intent
or prove that a miner deliberately manufactured a trajectory.

Individual disputed audit reports may be temporarily deferred under an explicit,
expiring ROOT-signed diagnostic record tied to the original job, report, worker,
miner, checkpoint and diagnostic digest. Their original verdicts remain intact;
deferral neither marks them verified nor applies an invalid-sample penalty. It
does not widen sampling tolerances. All other evidence and reward rules continue
unchanged. An expired unresolved disposition falls back to the last authenticated
assessment rather than silently declaring the disputed sample fraudulent.

The sole validator writer continues submitting the best authenticated assessment
each hour, with six-hour contribution half-life and current hotkey-to-UID mapping.
Inactive miners can retain decaying credit for earlier eligible contributions;
this does not award new contribution for epochs in which they submitted nothing.
Training failure, an unfinished epoch or unavailable fresh evidence must not stop
it. It retains the last valid assessment and confirmed penalties. A new model
run does not reset historical reward evidence or its transaction cursor. Burn
and owner-only fallbacks are prohibited. Commit-reveal may delay on-chain
visibility; uncertain transactions are reconciled rather than blindly replayed.

## Learning rule and initial capacity

The trainer admits authenticated, structurally complete groups after regenerating
their native prompts and grading their outcomes. **GRPO packing requires sampling
authenticity:** a group that is unaudited/pending or that fails TOPLOC/sampling
verification is excluded from the train pack (verified-or-nothing). Structural
seal and native grading may still complete without waiting for audits; only the
verified subset is packed for training. Grader/infrastructure errors defer sealing
rather than manufacturing failures. Flip credit uses the same fail/unverified
strip rule and never submits all-zero weights.

The GRPO objective reuses pinned XiaomiMiMo/verl reference functions from commit
`a2ad9f6160b03ff2d47e59832bfb6b289f37c917`, with explicit Affine adaptations:

| Setting | Initial operational value |
| --- | --- |
| Attempts per task | 8 canonical attempts; reference recipe uses 16 |
| Optimizer batch | Up to 32 distinct eligible tasks, at most 256 trajectories |
| Reference batch comparison | Released recipe uses 64 tasks x16 =1,024 trajectories |
| Group rewards | Correct 1; completed wrong 0; unresolved 0 |
| Advantage | Reward minus mean reward over all 8; no standard-deviation division |
| Loss weighting | Active-token mean within each task group, then equal task-group mean |
| PPO objective | Ratio clip 0.8–1.2; negative-advantage dual clip 3.0 |
| PPO epochs / optimizer updates | One epoch and one accumulated update per selected epoch batch |
| OLD probabilities | Trusted frozen-input trainer prefill; never miner-supplied denominators |
| Training probability convention | Raw temperature 1 model log probabilities; no top-k/top-p renormalization |
| Explicit KL / entropy coefficients | 0 / 0, matching the released reference configuration |
| Optimizer | PyTorch AdamW, CPU FP32 masters/moments, FP32 gradient accumulation |
| Learning rate | Constant 1e-6, no warmup |
| Adam betas / epsilon | 0.9,0.999 / 1e-8 |
| Weight decay | 0.01 for ordinary weights; zero for biases and one-dimensional tensors |
| Global gradient norm clip | 1.0, once after accumulation |

The initial 32-task ceiling is an operational setting pending measured long-output
training and publication timing. The implementation's 512-task ceiling is not a
claim that the first epoch trains 512 tasks. It is also not a set of successive
64-task updates. Microbatching reduces execution memory while preserving the
globally defined task weights and one optimizer step.

Unresolved attempts retain reward 0 in the all-N group mean, but all their policy
tokens are masked under `affine-unresolved-zero-reward-mask-all-v1`. They remain
in the stored inputs and cannot meet the wrong-answer minimum. This is an
explicit Affine adaptation, not a claim about an undocumented upstream grader.
Both positive and completed-wrong trajectories carry policy gradients. This is
GRPO, not the old pairwise preference loss or positive-only SFT.

The actor remains unchanged while OLD values and gradients are accumulated.
The ratio remains differentiable even when its initial numerical value is one.
The trainer checks numerical consistency and records loss/ratio/gradient metrics.
Its optimizer state stays durable locally; publication uploads the new model
and reports, not the optimizer. A retry after publication recovers the original
transaction instead of applying the same gradient update again.

Collection initially targets 30 minutes; the target is a complete epoch in under
one hour. Actual signed start/deadline and measured stage times are authoritative,
not a service-level guarantee in this guide. Audits have independent deadlines
and must not hold back training or checkpoint publication. A fresh model download
can consume part of the first collection window; the nine-group cap does not
promise that a new miner can finish nine groups in that window.

## Evaluation, evidence and troubleshooting

Track matched base and trained checkpoints on a fixed held-out suite using the
same native source, runtime, task list, seed, sampler and length policy. Changing
any of those can change the evaluator's dataset identity and draws. The previous
7B curves and private baselines under different grader sources remain separate.
The fresh base on this fixed32 suite solved18/32 (56.25%), with3 completed wrong
and11 unresolved outputs and no infrastructure errors. The original report is
faed31885f214f1d2de6d858ac5f419b7be7bdac8bdd62ba305759b3a6ca0507.
The matched private comparison has now completed: after one GRPO update on
two task groups, checkpoint037cf62a solved18/32 again, with1 completed wrong
and13 unresolved outputs (report77c256970f839bbf19938620dc8d39e2ee935694fe239e3fdef9aceddeeddeb5).
This shows no accuracy gain and is too small to establish a learning trend.
The public run starts from the original base, not that private checkpoint.
The first public update trained32 distinct task groups and published checkpoint
b756440a2d1831dbb6b2b7f15b081ad5430133977ddd82f9eb00eed71dcb12b0.
Its matched public fixed32 evaluation scored19/32 correct,1 completed wrong,
12 unresolved and0 errors, versus the public base's18/32,3 wrong,11 unresolved.
The exact tasks, prompts, common random draws, grader and runtime match.
Five tasks became correct while four previously correct tasks became unresolved.
This one-task net gain on32 tasks is an early observation, not an established trend.
Public base report SHA256:
ce16a508f8743afe2799446660a548768e4bd425811ffd75af61d2cd71904439.
Post-update report SHA256:
d83134457b93ac970e404a62aa6ead35305bf6fe3003b97c3ca56f60c66a5e3b.
An offline matched formatting diagnostic on these same64 original outputs
scores22/32 for BOTH checkpoints when single final boxes permit a terminal
period and correctly attached math wrappers. This is not the live grading rule;
original scores and signed evidence remain unchanged. Units, repeated boxes,
truncated answers and reasoning correctness were not silently accepted. The
diagnostic shows that formatting contributes to apparent gains and losses.
The second public checkpoint6e02820b scored21/32 correct,2 wrong,9 unresolved
and0 errors on the same fixed32 suite. Report SHA256:
64b7506a9585ddb194f76790112f5a7bfbdba1ea2b23a9ff917d8c1faf331ae6.
The matched narrow-format diagnostic across all96 original outputs remains
22/32 ->22/32 ->22/32, versus official18/32 ->19/32 ->21/32. This still does
not demonstrate a sustained improvement in math performance. A separate matched
128-task comparison is running with the original v1 grading on both checkpoints.
The third public checkpoint26887685 scored22/32 correct,2 wrong,8 unresolved
and0 errors;27 responses ended with EOS and5 reached the token budget. Report:
784ed0ce752569f8944c94f16427eac4ffe23d32c982332de75585b860746179.
The same offline narrow-format diagnostic now scores22/32 ->22/32 ->22/32
->25/32 across base and three updates. Relative to base, official outcomes have
8 gains and4 losses; the diagnostic has4 gains and1 loss. This is encouraging
small-sample evidence, not statistically established or sustained improvement.
Two former budget-capped outputs now complete correctly; another previously
wrong divisibility answer is correct. The larger independent128 comparison
remains pending and compares BASE with STEP2, not this third checkpoint.
The first two public updates trained63 distinct tasks across64 task slots.
Their data-quality and objective review, including incomplete-output masking
and later audit findings, is published at:
https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MIMO_FIRST_TWO_PUBLIC_UPDATES.md
Current GitHub also contains prospective optimizer-hash reuse and a report
receipt-clock fix. These do not replace the approved source archive above;
source migration and qualification precede activation.
The historical22/32 result used a different task-definition fingerprint and
cannot replace this matched baseline.
Fresh training-fit diagnostics are also separate from held-out generalization.
Neither a completed update, a lower training loss nor miner success quotas prove
learning. No convergence or sustained-improvement claim is made by this release.

Finalized evidence is published through the existing signed history format:
https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FINALIZED_EPOCH_EVIDENCE.md
It can link compact actual training inputs, exclusions, update metrics and
per-task evaluations. Verify the ROOT signature and artifact SHA256; gzip hashes
cover compressed bytes. GET-only links expire and are renewed. Missing evidence
is unavailable, not zero. Never publish open-epoch submissions or credentials.

- Closed discovery: wait for a valid signed opening. Do not bypass the deadline.
- Missing capability: check current UID, Ed25519 activation and next-epoch snapshot.
- Runtime/source/hash mismatch: install the advertised runtime and source; never
  edit the signed manifest or substitute a similarly named wheel/checkpoint.
- No eligible group: inspect all-N outcomes. At least one completed correct and
  one completed wrong are required; capped/missing-final attempts do not count.
- Local budget below N: raise the local ceiling; keep actual nonces exactly 0..7.
- Failed upload: retain the original prepared bytes/state and retry within the
  signed deadline. Generation before the deadline does not authorize a late upload.
- Child failure: retain logs/state and the original commitment; do not reset the
  journal or launch overlapping workers to duplicate an issued epoch.

new sampler, outcomes, proof transport or runtime.
